methodological_rigor.justification: This is a retrospective cohort of 136 pediatric RUNX1::RUNX1T1-positive AML patients who achieved morphologic CR after one induction course on AML-CAMS-2009/2016, with clearly defined 3-year OS and RFS endpoints. The modeling pipeline is coherent: LASSO with 10-fold cross-validation for variable selection followed by multivariable Cox regression, internal validation with 500 bootstrap resamples, and performance assessment via time-dependent ROC, calibration, DCA, and C-index. Methods for missingness are stated (random-forest imputation for variables with <10% missingness), and survival comparisons use Kaplan-Meier/log-rank with explicit handling of HSCT as not censored. Key limitations for a prediction model are that validation is internal only and the cohort is limited in size/events (22 deaths and 28 relapses), which increases overfitting risk despite bootstrapping.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The work is an individual retrospective cohort analysis developing prognostic nomograms for 3-year OS and RFS in a defined pediatric AML molecular subset, which maps to Oxford LoE 2b. The outcomes are patient-relevant (OS and relapse-free survival), and the predictors include clinically actionable factors such as MRD risk category, diagnostic WBC group (>=20x10^9/L), treatment regimen, and extramedullary infiltration for RFS. The manuscript reports that nomogram-derived scores stratify patients into distinct risk groups with significant OS/RFS differences, supporting potential use for post-remission risk-adapted management. The authors also explicitly note the need for prospective multicenter validation before clinical adoption, which fits the translational maturity of the model.

reporting_quality.justification: This is a multivariable prognostic prediction-model study, so TRIPOD is the closest applicable standard among the provided options. The manuscript reports key modeling and evaluation components (candidate variable domains, LASSO selection with cross-validation, multivariable Cox modeling, time-dependent ROC/calibration/DCA/C-index, and bootstrap internal validation) and defines OS/RFS and relapse criteria. However, it is not explicit about several TRIPOD-style items such as complete model specification for implementation (e.g., full coefficients/baseline hazard details) and external validation. Data and code sharing are not described in the provided normalized text, so reproducibility relies on narrative methods only.

novelty_literature.justification: The main contribution is an internally validated nomogram combining MRD risk, treatment regimen, diagnostic WBC group, and disease features (including flow-cytometry BM blast percentage and extramedullary infiltration for RFS) to predict 1- to 3-year OS/RFS in pediatric RUNX1::RUNX1T1-positive AML. This is a meaningful extension beyond single-factor prognostic reports by packaging predictors into deployable risk scores and performing discrimination/calibration and decision-curve evaluation. The novelty is limited by reliance on known prognostic domains in AML (MRD, leukocytosis, treatment intensity) rather than introducing a new biomarker or intervention. The manuscript itself positions the gap as prior pediatric studies being small/heterogeneous and focused on individual factors, which this modeling work addresses.

writing_presentation.justification: The abstract is quantitatively grounded (n=136; key predictors listed; internal validation via bootstrapping; performance assessed with ROC/calibration/DCA/C-index) and stays aligned with the stated aims. Methods and endpoints are described clearly, including explicit OS/RFS definitions and the handling of HSCT in survival analyses. The results section reports concrete cohort characteristics and event counts (22 deaths, 28 relapses) and ties them to the modeling goals. Some details that would improve usability for readers are a more implementation-ready presentation of the final nomogram equations and clearer delineation of what is available in supplementary materials.

key_strengths: Clinically relevant endpoints (3-year OS and RFS) with explicit relapse definitions in a clearly defined pediatric RUNX1::RUNX1T1-positive AML cohort (n=136).
Appropriate time-to-event modeling workflow (LASSO screening, multivariable Cox, time-dependent ROC/calibration/DCA, 500x bootstrap internal validation).
Risk stratification based on nomogram-derived scores with Kaplan-Meier separation, supporting potential clinical decision support.
key_concerns: No external or prospective validation; with 22 deaths and 28 relapses, overfitting remains a concern despite bootstrapping.
Limited implementation detail for deployment (e.g., full coefficient tables/baseline hazard or a calculator), which weakens TRIPOD completeness.
Single setting/serial-trial context may limit generalizability across centers with different MRD assays and consolidation strategies.
chief_reviewer.rationale: Methodology and clinical relevance are strong for a retrospective prediction-model paper, but lack of external validation keeps it below top-tier. With minor reporting/implementation clarifications and stronger discussion of generalizability, it is plausible for a tier-2 journal.
